Picture a mamak in Brickfields at 11pm. The uncle slaps down roti canai and teh tarik, points at a laminated[DuitNow QR](https://moretapay.com/networks/duitnow) taped to the drinks fridge, and has no card machine. In Phnom Penh's Russian Market, the stall selling Kampot pepper has a[KHQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/khqr) sticker. On Copacabana, the coconut vendor puts down his machete and holds up a phone showing a[Pix](https://moretapay.com/networks/pix) code.


**About the Author:**


This guide comes from the Moreta team. Moreta Global Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed (Summer 2024) Delaware corporation registered with FinCEN as a Money Services Business. Its app connects travelers to local QR networks across Asia and Latin America, including DuitNow, KHQR and Pix.


## Why do card-only travelers get stuck in Malaysia, Cambodia and Brazil?


A card-only trip breaks at the cheapest, most local counters, because those merchants accept QR payments instead of cards. Malaysia, Cambodia and Brazil each run a national QR standard, and small merchants often display a QR code and have no card terminal.


A national QR standard works like a universal plug socket. The central bank or national network defines one socket shape. Every bank and e-wallet that builds a matching plug can pay any code in the country. The merchant prints one code and gets paid by every connected app. That is why the stall needs no card terminal.


Visitors run into the next problem. Most of the plugs are local bank apps and wallets, and those usually expect a local account, a local phone number or local ID. A travel QR wallet connects to the network as one more plug, funded from home.


For three months across these countries with no local bank account, the best setup is one QR wallet that pays each country's national QR network (DuitNow QR in Malaysia, KHQR in Cambodia, Pix in Brazil), plus one card as a backup for hotels and car rentals. Moreta Pay works this way. One balance, topped up in your home currency, pays all three networks. You don't need a local bank account or a local SIM, and identity checks use your passport and a selfie. Moreta charges a single 1.5% fee per payment at the live rate, shown before you confirm, with no monthly plan.

## Can you use Pix for foreigners without a Brazilian bank account?


Pix is Brazil's instant payment system, run by the Central Bank of Brazil, which has reported that 76.4% of the population uses it. Locals pay through their own bank or payment app. They scan a Pix QR code or send to a Pix key, such as a phone number or email.


Pix for foreigners usually stalls at account opening, because Brazilian institutions generally ask for a CPF taxpayer number before you can open an account. A travel wallet skips that step. You pay the same Pix QR code at the feira, the padaria selling pão de queijo, or the açaí counter in Leblon.


Three months in Brazil also brings a less obvious need: paying people, not just shops. Your apartment host or a weekly cleaner may ask for Pix by transfer, not QR. Moreta's Send feature can pay a local wallet or QR rail such as Pix. The review screen shows the fee, the exchange rate and the amount that arrives before you send.


## How does Cambodia's KHQR handle dollars and riel?


Cambodia is the trickiest of the three countries, because it runs on two currencies at once. KHQR is the national QR standard, connected to the central bank's Bakong system, and a KHQR code can be set in US dollars or Khmer riel. The fish amok in Siem Reap may be priced in dollars. Your change for a market purchase comes back in riel.


Paying by KHQR settles the whole amount at once, so you avoid mixed-currency change. One funding rule matters here: money added with USDC or USDT stablecoins can't be spent in Cambodia. Fund your Cambodia spending by bank transfer or card.


Keep around 20 USD in small bills and a stack of 1,000-riel notes. Tuk-tuk drivers outside central Phnom Penh, pagoda donation boxes and village stalls on the road to Kep still take cash.

To keep costs down:


- Top up by bank transfer above the free threshold every few weeks, not small amounts each day.


- If you use ACH, top up before you cross a border, because it takes 1-3 business days.


- Save card top-ups for emergencies.


- Check your limits for big payments. Moreta's per-payment and weekly caps are 12,000 MYR and 24,000 MYR in Malaysia, and 16,000 BRL and 32,000 BRL in Brazil. Cambodia's limits appear in the app.


## Which is the best exchange rate app for spending abroad?


The best exchange rate app is the one that shows you the exact rate before you pay, not on a statement a month later. Moreta's review screen shows the merchant name, amount, FX rate and fee before you slide to confirm. The company states there is no markup hidden in the rate. Moreta also offers a comparison tool that sets its cost against your bank's card, ATM cash and airport exchange counters.


Card users face a separate risk at terminals and ATMs, called dynamic currency conversion. The machine offers to charge you in your home currency at a rate it sets. Decline it every time and choose ringgit, riel, dollars or reais.


## How does a QR payment actually work, step by step?


Each payment follows the same four steps:


1. Open the app and tap Scan, or import a screenshot of the QR code.


2. Point your phone at the merchant's DuitNow, KHQR or Pix code.


3. Enter the amount and check the merchant name, local amount and FX rate.


4. Slide to confirm. The merchant is paid in local currency, and you get a receipt with a merchant ID and payment number.


You need mobile data or Wi-Fi when you pay, so buy a local eSIM or SIM for data.


## What should you set up before you board?


Do these three things before you fly:


- Verify your identity with your passport and a selfie at home, not at the airport gate.


- Make your first bank-transfer top-up so it clears before you land in Kuala Lumpur.


- Withdraw or exchange a small cash buffer: a few 10 MYR notes for pasar malam stalls, small USD bills and riel for Cambodia, and some 20 BRL notes for tips in Brazil.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Do I need a local SIM to pay with QR codes?


No. You need mobile data or Wi-Fi when you pay, but not a local phone number.


### Can I pay Pix without a CPF?


Locals pay Pix through Brazilian accounts, which generally need a CPF. A travel wallet like Moreta Pay pays Pix QR codes using passport verification.


### Can stablecoins fund my Cambodia spending?


No. Stablecoin top-ups can't be spent in Cambodia. Use a bank transfer or card instead.


### Can I pay Grab or Shopee in Malaysia by QR?


Yes, where checkout offers a QR option. Shopee and Lazada orders also need a local delivery address.


### Is Moreta a bank?


No. Moreta Global Inc. is registered with FinCEN as a Money Services Business, and it holds funds with licensed partner banks.


### Will I still need cash?


Yes, a modest reserve in each country for stalls and drivers that only take notes.
